q: How do you choose chunk size?
a: Start around 300–800 tokens with 10–20% overlap based on document type, then measure: build question → gold passage pairs and compare retrieval recall@k and answer quality across a few sizes. Stay within the embedding model's input limit.

q: What chunking strategies do you know?
a: Fixed-size with overlap, recursive (paragraph → sentence → word), structure-aware (headings, sections, tables), semantic (split where topic similarity drops), parent–child / small-to-big, sentence-window, and contextual chunking (prepend document context to each chunk).

q: Why not use very large chunks?
a: One vector for a large chunk averages many topics, so similarity to a specific question weakens and retrieval precision drops; fewer chunks fit the prompt; more irrelevant tokens raise cost and distract the model. Parent–child retrieval gives small-chunk precision with large-chunk context.
So information that spans a boundary (a sentence split between two chunks) appears complete in at least one chunk. Too much overlap causes duplicate results and a bigger index.
Index small child chunks for precise matching, but when one matches, return its larger parent section (or neighbouring chunks) to the LLM so it has enough context to answer.
